<reason>B made the stronger comparison: peak limits combined with suitable alternatives can reduce excess pressure without making landmarks unpopular. It directly answered the percentage and housing-enforcement questions, acknowledging uncertainty and limiting promotion to protected, equipped districts. A raised legitimate infrastructure and displacement concerns, but repeatedly assumed redistribution must add visits rather than replace them. Its insistence that most visitors must abandon the hubs imposed a stronger burden than the proposition requires and left B’s marginal-relief case standing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s distinction between flexibility and additional demand was decisive: someone able to travel in May might otherwise choose July. A never justified excluding that substitution, despite direct questioning. B also effectively distinguished a fully booked attraction from an overloaded surrounding district.</best_rebuttal>
